# Synapse 2.0.4

A fix release: the browser opens again on Windows, an Evaluator step reads what earlier steps wrote, and two security fixes.

## Security

- **Google sign-in is bound to the sign-in that started it.** When connecting Google Workspace, the callback did not check the sign-in's `state`, so another person's Google account could be made an install's Google connection under narrow conditions. Each sign-in now has its own one-time state, and starting one needs your Synapse session. See the security advisory for details. Affects all releases before 2.0.4.
- **The backend listens on this computer only.** `synapse start` now binds the backend to `127.0.0.1`; the app you open in the browser is unchanged, so opening Synapse from your phone on the same Wi-Fi still works. Set `SYNAPSE_BACKEND_HOST=0.0.0.0` if you need the backend itself reachable from other devices. Docker images keep listening inside their container as before.
- **Metrics need a token.** `/api/v2/metrics` now answers only with `METRICS_TOKEN` (or the app's own token), as its description always said.

## Fixed

- **The browser works on Windows.** On Windows, "Keep me signed in", "Record a task" and any agent that uses the browser failed with an error, because the browser's helper process was started without the system settings Windows needs to run a program. It now starts with them, and every other helper Synapse starts uses the same list, with a check that keeps it that way.
- **A browser that can't start says why.** If the browser still can't start, the dialog shows what it reported instead of a bare error, and agents get the same sentence.
- **An Evaluator reads what earlier steps wrote.** `{{ state.x }}` in an Evaluator's prompt or route descriptions is now filled in, so an Evaluator after a Human step sees the person's reply rather than the placeholder. The Evaluator prompt gets the same `{{` suggestions as other prompts.
- **A missing value is said, not passed on.** When a prompt names a value that isn't there (a field a step didn't write, or an unknown variable), the model now reads a short note saying so, instead of the raw `{{ … }}`.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.4`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
